# T6.08: HEVC rate control

`setup_hevc` fills `nvenc_h265_rc_s` the way the H.264 path fills its RC (M3, T3.06-T3.08): NAL HRD, `maxQPD` 6 /
`baseQPD` 3, frame rate x 256, CPB size and peak rate, `Np` from the IDR period, `Ravg` = `R` = bits per pixel per frame
in 23.8 fixed point, `i_size_ratio` 1/1, `single_frame_vbv` 0 (T3.08). The rate-control mode goes in
`SET_CONTROL_PARAMS` as for H.264.

`encodeN -hevc 1920 1080 120 25 28 1` (moving synthetic content), frames 10-119:

| mode | target | result | largest P | QP | luma | decode errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CBR (`RC=2`) | 8 Mbit/s | 8.07 Mbit/s (+0.9 %) | 186.9 kbit | 23-26 | 50.64 dB | 0 |
| CBR | 20 Mbit/s | 20.50 Mbit/s (+2.5 %) | 487.7 kbit | 15-17 | 54.87 dB | 0 |
| CBR | 3 Mbit/s | 2.99 Mbit/s (-0.3 %) | 77.2 kbit | 36-46 | 35.27 dB | 0 |
| VBR (`RC=1`) | 8 avg / 12 max | 9.56 Mbit/s (between average and peak) | 211.2 kbit | 21-24 | 51.72 dB | 0 |
| low latency (`RC=18`, one-frame VBV 133,333 bits) | 8 Mbit/s | 7.68 Mbit/s (-4 %) | 148.9 kbit | 24-26 | 49.24 dB | 0 |

All within 10 % of the target. One difference from H.264: with the one-frame VBV the largest P frame (148.9 kbit) goes
12 % over the per-frame budget (H.264 stayed under it, T3.08); the average is under. Worth a look if Parsec shows
latency spikes with HEVC.
